newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fuji Heavy recalls more than 330,000 cars in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Fuji Heavy recalls more than 330,000 cars in Japan.

text.p: Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd said on Tuesday it had told the Transport Ministry it was recalling 336,384 cars in Japan to repair a fault that could cause the engines in the cars to stall.
Fuji Heavy has no estimate yet on the cost of the recall, the spokesman said, adding no accidents have been reported in Japan or abroad because of the defects.
The cars, made between December 29, 1988, and January 19, 1994, are Fuji Heavy's Impreza and Legacy and Isuzu Motors Ltd's Aska models, a Fuji Heavy spokesman said.
Aska is Isuzu's version of the Fuji Heavy-made Legacy and is sold only in Japan.
Fuji Heavy exported about 410,000 of the cars, including 350,000 to the United States, but did not say how many of those cars would be recalled.
It will also repair those cars free of charge in accordance with each country's rules, the spokesman said.
The defective part is a locking bolt on a pulley used for the alternator and power steering pump.
